newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: JSC blames price discounting for Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: JSC blames price discounting for Q1 loss.

text.p: Jefferson Smurfit Corporation (JSC) said on Thursday that the $7.0 million loss recorded in the first quarter of 1997 was caused primarily by price discounting in corrugated containers and in newsprint.
Longer-than-expected maintenance downtime at the Fernandina Beach linerboard mill also had a negative impact on the results, JSC said in a statement.

The company, which is 46.5 percent-owned by Irish-based paper and packaging manufacturer Jefferson Smurfit Plc, reported a loss per share of $0.06 compared with a profit of $0.48 in the first quarter of 1996.

"The domestic market for linerboard and medium remained in disarray in the first quarter as a result of a build-up in industry inventories that began in December," president and chief executive officer Richard Graham said.
This build-up caused steep discounting in containerboard prices which depressed the price of corrugated containers, he said.
Graham said demand for packaging was strong with Smurfit's quarterly container shipments rising by seven percent over year-earlier levels.
Company inventories of containerboard were at manageable levels as a result of the strong shipments and the downtime at Fernandina Beach, he said.
JSC's other packaging businesses, which include folding cartons and industrial and consumer packaging, performed within expectations during the quarter, he said.
Average newsprint prices were more than $250 below year-ago levels but the company announced a price increase during the quarter which took effect on April 1.
JSC said reclaimed fibre prices increased slightly compared to fourth quarter levels as rough winter weather forced many mills to shift their fibre mix to recycled material.
Graham said JSC's earnings would be under pressure in coming months as a result of the negative pricing trends in corrugated containers.

"On the positive side, demand for all packaging is strong and pricing in our non-container products is relatively stable. In addition, we should realise a significant benefit from the newsprint price increase," he said.

JSC said debt levels rose by around $10 million in the first quarter as the company completed the acquisition of a corrugated container plant in Florida from Tropicana and bought three Chicago-area recycling plants.
